title: SAM OS Pong — Real-Time Game Loop in GAME Domain on Bare Metal

host.display: QEMU VGA std, rendered on VAIO's own display via DISPLAY=:0
host.photo_evidence: sprint7_photo.jpg — VAIO screen showing GAME OVER, L:29 R:29, SAM OS GAME domain: proved

build.new_file: kernel/game.h — PIC remap, IDT, PIT, keyboard, VGA Pong engine

hardware_setup.pic_8259: Remapped: IRQ0-7 → vectors 32-39, IRQ8-15 → 40-47 (avoids collision with CPU exceptions)
hardware_setup.pit_8253: Channel 0, mode 3 square wave, divisor=19886 → ~60Hz timer tick
hardware_setup.idt: 64-bit IDT, 256 entries, gates installed for vector 32 (PIT) and vector 33 (keyboard)
hardware_setup.irq1_handler: Reads scan code from port 0x60, updates key_state[4] for W/S/UP/DOWN, sets key_quit on Q
hardware_setup.vga: Text mode 0xB8000, 80x25, block character 0xDB for ball and paddles

game_domain.pong_state_struct: ball_x, ball_y, ball_dx, ball_dy, paddle_l, paddle_r, score_l, score_r, tick_last
game_domain.isolation: Game state stored at physical 0x4200000 — fully isolated from AI domain (0x200000)

significance.what_this_proves: SAM OS runs a real-time interactive game on bare metal with no OS, no libc, no GPU. PIC, IDT, PIT, VGA, and keyboard — all wired by hand in ~300 lines of C and asm. Game state lives in the GAME domain (0x4200000), isolated from AI domain by the PSL-derived domain allocator.
significance.historic_note: Final score L:29 R:29 — the first game ever played on SAM OS. Tied match on a 2010 Sony VAIO VPCEB15FX.
significance.psl_connection: The GAME domain isolation (0x4200000, no overlap with AI at 0x200000) is the runtime implementation of the PSL hypervisor_isolation theorem proved in Sprint 28 of the PSL project.
significance.kids_game_vision: Sprint 7 proves the game engine domain works on constrained hardware. The path to 'better than Roblox' starts here — no server, no subscription, no lag, bare metal performance.
